reason: Comparison with the edition corrected the first reading's 'marie...' to 'maxime vero et epatis dolo[res]', 'dicit franciscum' to 'dicat secundum hanc seriem', and 'ad iugulares' to 'ad sa[gittidas]', and showed that the red lines are Hippocratic text, not rubrics.
sources: Thaddaeus Florentinus, Expositiones ... In praeclarum regiminis acutorum (Venice: Giunta, 1527), Regimen acutorum IV, Textus XIX-XX, pp. 333 and verso, MDZ bsb10139648 scans 709-710
Same edition, Textus XXIV-XXVII, p. 334 and verso, MDZ bsb10139648 scans 711-712
Galen, Opera, Impressio quinta (Venice: Giunta, 1522), vol. 3, Regimen acutorum IV Textus XIX, MDZ bsb10139501 scan 483 (OCR snippet only)
text:
SOURCE-ASSISTED READING of F-nfu2 (Antwerpen, EHC, Fragm. 308), made after comparison with Hippocrates, Regimen acutorum IV with Galen's commentary (Venice: Giunta 1527, MDZ bsb10139648 scans 709-712). Lines reread on the image by a research reader: face A red top (6 lines) and last two lines; face B top black block (6 lines), red blocks Textus XXV, XXVI, XXVII. The mid-face black commentary was not reread. Every line is cut at both ends. ( ) = expansion, [ ] = lost at the edge or supplied from the edition, ? = uncertain.
